cycles.notes: The most consequential finding of cycle 1 is the correction of the data-detective brief's name-attribution: Pam Smith is NOT the HHS Principal Deputy Asst Sec; that role belongs to Raissa Downs. The LDA covered_position field aggregates positions across all lobbyists on a filing, which produced the apparent overlap. Once corrected, the TDY cluster geometry is in fact STRONGER than the brief described: TWO of the three co-founders (Downs, Young) held the senior HHS Office of Legislation roles, and a third senior partner (Smith) was Staff Director of the Senate HELP Committee under Chair Harkin. The firm is documentably the institutional home for Medicare Part D architects who became drug-company lobbyists (ProPublica 2009), and its Sept 2025 acquisition by FGS Global is itself a market-structure event of note. The Vertex v. HHS-OIG active litigation is the strongest single claim for promotion to a Brownstein-Hyatt-parallel finding: a $6M+ client in active federal litigation against the agency where two of the firm's founders held senior legislative-affairs roles.
